claims.text: Conventional single-phase ZrB2 is typically processed above 2300 °C.
Earlier lower-temperature ZrB2 specimens were produced above 1700 °C.
Single-phase ZrB2 has excellent intrinsic strength but poor oxidation durability and liquid-metal corrosion resistance.
A minor amount of silicon can be retained within the solid-solubility limit of ZrB2 without forming secondary phases.
Silicon doping enables densification of ZrB2 by reactive spark plasma sintering at approximately 1700 °C.
Silicon enhances mass transport during lower-temperature densification of ZrB2.
Silicon segregates to ZrB2 grain boundaries and surfaces during densification.
Segregated silicon promotes formation of a contiguous silica or borosilicate protective oxide scale.
The silica-rich scale is stable and passivating under high-temperature exposure.
The silica-rich scale impedes oxygen ingress into silicon-doped ZrB2.
The silica-rich scale impedes penetration by liquid plating metal.
Low-level silicon doping maintains the strong Zr–B and B–B bonding within ZrB2 grains.
Silicon-doped ZrB2 processed at approximately 1700 °C will have strength and structural integrity comparable to conventional high-temperature and earlier lower-temperature ZrB2.
Silicon-doped ZrB2 processed at approximately 1700 °C will have significantly better oxidation resistance than both conventional high-temperature and earlier lower-temperature ZrB2.
Silicon-doped ZrB2 processed at approximately 1700 °C will be less susceptible to liquid plating-metal corrosion than both conventional high-temperature and earlier lower-temperature ZrB2.
The proposed oxidation benefit is expected to apply in oxidizing environments up to approximately 1200 °C.
The benefits depend on keeping silicon within its solubility limit and below the service-temperature regime in which the protective scale degrades.
